newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak c.bank says no refinancing repo on Thursday.
newsitem.headline: Slovak c.bank says no refinancing repo on Thursday.

text.p: The National Bank of Slovakia (NBS) said it would not hold any refinancing repo tender on Thursday as the local banking sector appeared to have enough crown liquidity to meet minimum reserves requirements.
"We will not refinance the sector today, since the market liquidity seems to be sufficient," said Peter Andresic, Head of the NBS Open Market Operation Department.
"On the contrary, we might sell some state treasury bills from our portfolio later on Thursday to draw some liquidity from the market," Andreasic said.
He added that the central bank was now analysing possible market liquidity flows, mainly potential inflows or outflows from or to the finance ministry accounts.
According to NBS figures, the Slovak banking sector as of July 30 met its minimum reserves requirements 100 percent.
The daily volume of minimum reserves for commercial banks total 36.583 billion crowns in the current reserves period ending July 31.
The central bank monitors market liquidity on a daily basis and decides each morning whether to hold any open market operations.
The NBS on Wednesday added 1.5 billion crowns into the local money market through a one-week repo tender with an average rate falling to 15.55 percent from 16.30 percent in a similar repo on Tuesday.
